I really think the tactic is *improved* by removing this from the scope.  I laid out my thoughts here
https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/287929-mathlib4/topic/Narrowing.20the.20scope.20of.20.60linear_combination.60/near/462845544
(and let's continue the discussion there rather than here), but for the record, let me write precisely what I think that scope should be:

`linear_combination` is a tactic which reduces problems of the form
```
h₁ : a₁ = b₁
h₂ : a₂ = b₂
h₃ : a₃ = b₃
⊢ A = B
```
to the task of showing that 
```
(f a₁ a₂ a₃ - f b₁ b₂ b₃) - (A - B)
```
equals zero (and then tries a standard normalization procedure to check that).  I believe the scope of the tactic should be limited to operations `f` for which this is the same thing as
```
f (a₁ - b₁) (a₂ - b₂) (a₃ - b₃) - (A - B)
```
Namely, **ℤ-linear** operations `f`.

This puts the error message on the whole tactic, not just the `linear_combination`, right?

If so, presumably Kyle's suggestion [on Zulip](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/270676-lean4/topic/Propagating.20errors.20through.20Unhygienic.2Erun/near/464484715) would resolve it.

It's reasonable to import `AlgebraicIndependent`. But for the proof there is still some way to go...

> I think this can be decomposed into two facts:
> 
> 1. if `i : R →+* A` makes A a flat R-algebra, then `f : R[X]` is transcendental over R implies that `f.map i : A[X]` is transcendental over A. (The converse holds when `i` is injective. More generally, R[X] can be replaced by any R-algebra and A[X] by its tensor product with A.) In the current situation, `A = R[s] = supported R s` is free over R, so we can avoid importing flatness.

Yeah, that was what I said in https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/144837-PR-reviews/topic/Transcendental.20and.20algebraically.20independent/near/480005599 . Note that the current proof in this PR does not require flatness or freeness, as it rearranges the aeval map as composition of several maps, and uses the fact that `[Mv]Polynomial.map` preserves injectivity.

> 2. If `f : A →ₐ[R] B` is injective, then `x : A` is transcendental over R iff `f x` is. This is equivalent to [isAlgebraic_algHom_iff](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/RingTheory/Algebraic.html#isAlgebraic_algHom_iff), and in the current situation there is an injective R[s]-AlgHom from R[s][X] to R[σ] that sends `f.map (algebraMap R R[s])` to `Polynomial.aeval (X i : MvPolynomial σ R) f`.

That is `AlgebraicIndependent.ringHom_of_comp_eq` etc. in PR #18648. I haven't added `AlgHom` version yet.

I realized I was not using the good convention regarding `<;>`. I opened a [discussion on Zulip](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Chaining.20.3C.3B.3E/with/520757779) which yield better proofs. Feel free to roam through the discussion and pick you favorite. Here are two examples:
```suggestion
  obtain ⟨s, hs, h₁, h₂⟩ := hahn_decomposition ν μ
  refine ⟨s, hs, ?_, ?_⟩
  all_goals
    rw [Measure.le_iff]
    intros
    simp [*]
```
```suggestion
  obtain ⟨s, hs, h₁, h₂⟩ := hahn_decomposition ν μ
  use s, hs <;> simp +contextual [Measure.le_iff, *]
```

~~refer to our private discussion; `@[simps!]` cannot reduce through the coercion `(taylorEquiv r : R[X] ≃ₗ[R] R[X])` (originally an `AlgEquiv`).~~

Edit: this works but the backward version does not, see [#mathlib4 > Quickfix: symm version missing from `semilinearEquiv`](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Quickfix.3A.20symm.20version.20missing.20from.20.60semilinearEquiv.60/with/521522817) for more info.

Another suggestion for the notation is to remove the `[𝕜]` argument

In SciLean, the derivative notation does not state the base field explicitly. It is expected that you usually work with one base field and state that with `set_default_scalar  𝕜` at the top of the file which just defines local notation `defaultScalar%` that expands to `𝕜` and the notation uses `defaultScalar%`
```
macro "set_default_scalar" r:term : command =>
  `(local macro_rules | `(defaultScalar%) => do pure (← `($r)).raw)
```

This is Kyle's solution discussed here https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/270676-lean4/topic/notation.20over.20field/with/419274309 

Adding something like `defaultScalar%` should be done as separate PR and then we can add an option to omit `𝕜` in the notation.

Since we currently do not have a consistent way to work with terminal objects, I've opted for the following approach:
```lean
section Terminal

def isTerminalOf (T : C) (ht : IsTerminal T) : IsTerminal ((of C).obj T) :=
  IsTerminal.ofUniqueHom (fun _ ↦ ⟨fun _ ↦ PUnit.unit, fun _ ↦ ht.from _⟩)
    (fun _ _ ↦ hom_ext (funext fun _ ↦ rfl) (fun _ ↦ ht.hom_ext _ _))

instance [HasTerminal C] : HasTerminal (FormalCoproduct.{w} C) :=
  (isTerminalOf (⊤_ C) terminalIsTerminal).hasTerminal

end Terminal
```
